key_decisions: --no-deps on the curated install is LOAD-BEARING, not an optimisation. python_deps.txt is the complete closure MINUS the engine-owned torch stack and MINUS the duplicate cv2 builds; with deps, pip re-derives all of them from diffusers/ultralytics/albumentations and undoes both removals.

The torch family is excluded from the RESOLVE, not just the emit. `uv pip compile --no-emit-package torch` still emitted pinned triton, 16 nvidia-* wheels and (Linux) cuda-toolkit/cuda-bindings/cuda-pathfinder, all `# via torch` — this card's own Evidence A stack, reproduced by our generator. scripts/compile-node-deps.mjs filters the whole family post-compile. nvidia-ml-py is deliberately KEPT (pure-Python NVML, ultralytics needs it, no CUDA runtime).

opencv unified to opencv-contrib-python-headless. Three nodes declared three distributions into the same cv2 namespace and pipPins forced TWO at once, so `import cv2` is last-writer-wins on every engine shipped so far. mediapipe/ultralytics/albumentations pull the other three TRANSITIVELY, which is the second reason --no-deps is required.

cupy dropped entirely, zero behaviour change: measured cupy ABSENT and taichi ABSENT in the live engine with Frame-Interpolation loading fine; it is reachable only via vfi_models/ops, which no eagerly-imported model __init__ touches, and we ship only RIFE VFI. cupy-wheel is a 2.9kB source shim whose setup.py imports pkg_resources — it fails to build on every platform on every fresh install and reports success anyway (os.system ignores the exit code).

pipPins and installRequirementsCommand were KEPT on the dep entries even though the local path no longer reads them: routes/remoteModels.js:412-417 still sends install_command/pip_pins to the Pod wrapper. Deleting them before the Pod converges would break remote.

Phase 1 (PIP_CONSTRAINT for the local engine) is now nearly a no-op and is a close-as-superseded candidate. runPipCommand has exactly ONE call site left in the whole local engine and it runs --no-deps against a file with no torch in it, so it structurally cannot move torch. What remains unconstrained is comfy-cli's own pip during `comfy install` — already guarded on macOS (pinned torch first + --skip-torch-or-directml) and moot on Windows (prebuilt archive, no pip). A Linux-only sliver.
constraints: NOT VERIFIED: no real-engine install has ever run against the curated set, and ComfyUI has never booted against it. Evidence so far is throwaway venvs only. The card's own verify needs a CPU/Linux box: grep -icE "downloading (triton|nvidia)" = 0, torch reports a +cpu tag, "Requirement already satisfied" count far below 400, zero IMPORT FAILED. The user HAS a Linux box available next session — run it.
A Pod IMAGE BUILD is USER-AUTHORIZED, and live Pod ops are USER-ONLY. Do not build or start anything on mpi-ci without asking. Use the build-pod-image skill when the user approves.
mpi-ci is a SEPARATE git repo at c:/AI/Mpi/mpi-ci/. Use `git -C` or cd; never run git from Cubric-Vision against it. Absolute paths in all tool calls.

Pod runtime edits (wrapper.py / start.sh) are NOT an image rebuild — they are R2-floated on two channels: ./publish-runtime.sh dev → restart Pod → test → ./publish-runtime.sh promote. NEVER publish-runtime.sh stable for day-to-day work. So the wrapper half of this convergence may not need a rebuild at all; only the Dockerfile bake half does.

The Pod already sets ENV PIP_CONSTRAINT=/opt/constraints.txt (cu130 trio) AND ENV PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL=.../whl/cu130 — the latter because the constraint pins a LOCAL version (+cu130) that exists only on the pytorch index, so isolated build envs would otherwise hit ResolutionImpossible (MPI-342). Keep both when converging.

The Pod build already greps for IMPORT FAILED (MPI-341) — that is the safety net that makes a hand-curated set safe. It is the gate that will catch an under-specified python_deps.txt, so converging the Pod is also what finally proves Phase 2.
Regenerating the lock needs network (fetches node requirements + core requirements from GitHub) and `uv` on PATH. uv 0.6.0 is what is installed here.
